title: U.S. envoys Kushner, Witkoff meet with Putin at Kremlin in talks to end Russia-Ukraine war

Witkoff and fellow American envoy Jared Kushner were set to talk later in the day with Ukraine's president. (Vyacheslav Prokofiev/Sputnik/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys met with President Vladimir Putin on Thursday as Washington sought new momentum in peace efforts after two days of U.S.-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian delegations.
U.S. envoys fly from Russia to Ireland to brief Zelenskyy after speaking to Putin

U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys met on Thursday with President Vladimir Putin as Washington sought new momentum in peace efforts after two days of U.S.-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian delegations.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Trump's son-in-law, brokered the talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, the first direct discussions between representatives of Moscow and Kyiv in nine months as the push for peace stalled.
The two days of talks that ended on Wednesday produced no major breakthrough, aside from an agreement to swap a large number of prisoners, with the exact figure still to be announced.

Kushner and Witkoff met with Putin at the Kremlin and are scheduled to fly later to Dublin, Ireland, for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, as Moscow's full-scale invasion nears the five-year mark.

Kushner said that one of the goals of the meeting with Putin was to get the Russian leader's blessing for European representatives to be part of the talks, which are looking at the continent's broader security arrangements.
The U.S. and Zelenskyy want Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.

But Moscow doesn't want European countries involved in the direct negotiations, complaining they are financing and supplying Ukraine's war effort. The Europeans are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, and whether the U.S. will be too accommodating to Kremlin demands.

Putin again warns against European troops

Many in Europe see the inclusion of Moscow in discussions about postwar European security as an unwelcome concession to Putin, who has described NATO's eastward expansion as a main security threat to Russia. Putin has demanded the transatlantic alliance's troops be pulled back from Russia's borders.
Some analysts say negotiators may be looking to grant Russia concessions on NATO's strategy in return for peace in Ukraine — a possibility that alarms European leaders.

items: Russia-Ukraine talks mediated by U.S. end with news of 'good momentum,' large-scale prisoner swap

blocks.text: Putin reaffirmed to the U.S. envoys Moscow's rejection of any European troop presence in Ukraine in a post-war scenario, saying that Russia sees them as a threat to its security and warns that they would be legitimate targets.
He also said Russia sees its border with Ukraine as the line of control — a reference to Moscow's claim over the four Ukrainian regions that Moscow annexed in 2022 but never fully captured.
Zelenskyy is in Dublin for a meeting of more than 40 European countries that also includes NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was also present.
Rutte said the U.S., Europe and Ukraine are "very much aligned" on what security guarantees should look like, following a meeting in Paris in January.
"But now of course we need the peace deal, or at least a ceasefire," Rutte said.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stands next to French President Emmanuel Macron, centre, and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney as they pose for a photo along with other leaders at the European Political Community (EPC) Summit in Dublin, Ireland, on Thursday. (Peter Morrison/The Associated Press)
Zelenskyy called the proposed prisoner exchange a positive step but also insisted Ukraine won't surrender Russian-occupied territory in return for peace.
Russia and Ukraine have occasionally swapped prisoners, but both sides remain far apart in their terms for accepting a settlement.
Amid the negotiations, fighting continues along the 1,200-kilometre front line.

items: Putin pushes the myth of Russian invincibility, seemingly to set his terms for peace

blocks.text: Russia's bigger army has been held back by dogged Ukrainian resistance while Moscow's drone and missile strikes aim to deny civilians heat, electricity and running water, sapping public morale in what Kyiv calls a "weaponization of winter."
Zelenskyy says Starshield service disrupted again

Ukraine is experiencing another slowdown in the U.S. Starshield system — SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service — that the country needs to defend itself against Russian attacks, Zelenskyy said Thursday on social media.

Military units have recorded "significant disruptions," including speed restrictions limiting its drones to 161 kph, Zelenskyy said. He added that a military investigation established that the restrictions weren't random errors.
Ukraine uses Starlink and Starshield for intercepting Russian drones and launching its own mid- and long-range strikes.
Last month, limits on Ukrainian drone speeds severely disrupted operations and alarmed Kyiv officials who fear U.S. support could drop off.
Firefighters work on Thursday at an apartment building in Kyiv that was damaged following a Russian drone strike. (Gleb Garanich/Reuters)
SpaceX CEO Elon Musk acknowledged that his company had throttled the Starlink internet service in Ukraine for about a week, saying the system couldn't be used for offensive strikes against Russia.
Zelenskyy said in Dublin that the speed limits cover operations in Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine and that Kyiv is trying to find out from U.S. officials what is going on.
"If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going," he said.

Russia's Defence Ministry said its air defences downed 71 Ukrainian drones overnight. Its forces struck a drone-making plant in Kyiv and three other facilities producing missile fuel and drone components in the area around the Ukrainian capital, the ministry said.
Russia launched missiles and 123 drones, 73 of them jet-powered drones, at Ukraine overnight, the Ukrainian air force said. Hits were recorded at 17 locations, it said.
